en: Preface to the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chijue of Mount Jing.
After Chan Master Chijue of Mount Jing had passed into nirvana, his disciple Liaoyuan presented a compilation of the Master’s lifelong teachings and exhortations to You Yu of Xishan, saying:
"You are one who knows our Master; why not provide a preface so that these words may be transmitted? I...
In my later years, I came to know this Master; having obtained several of his phrases for my own use, I no longer declined [his instructions].

I have observed that the recorded sayings (*yulu*) of the venerable masters of recent times have mostly fallen into fixed patterns. Only Master Chijue stands out slightly; for his realization was transcendent and his application was unencumbered.
Thus, throughout his life, he did not permit others to offer words in his room, focusing exclusively on this: "To catch the dragon, one must strike."
As for the "Phoenix," few scholars have been able to find their way into its domain. Its gate and courtyard are lofty and steep, standing as the radiant spiritual light of a patriarchal master.
Now it has passed away; only the traces of its sword remain. Were it not for those of the same lineage, who could recognize the bitterness of its toil?
There must surely be those who will protect and uphold it, so that it may circulate for a long time. Written on the Dragon Boat Festival of the Xinhai year of the Chunyou era by Mushi.
Table of Contents for the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chijue,

The Record of the Chan Monastery Baoen Guangxiao in Jiaxing Prefecture;
The Record of the Chan Monastery Taiping Xingguo at Mount Jiangshan in Jiankang Prefecture;
The Record of the Chan Monastery Chongsheng on Snow Peak.
Recorded Sayings of Tiantong Jingde Chan Monastery, Qingyuan Prefecture;
Recorded Sayings of Lingyin Chan Monastery, Lin’an Prefecture;
and the Founding Record of Juechengshan Fahua Chan Monastery, Pingjiang Prefecture.
Recorded Sayings of the Xingsheng Wanshou Chan Temple at Mount Jing, Lin’an Prefecture;
Volume Lower: Universal Dharma Discourses, Eulogies, and Verses.
Supplementary Notes to the Epitaph and Biographical Account of the Universal Dharma-Master Fanguan:
Volume One of the Recorded Sayings of Master Chijue.
Recorded by Attendant Zhìyī of the Verbal Record of Master Chījué during his tenure at Bào’ēn Guāngxiào Chán Temple in Jiāxìng Prefecture.
On the twentieth day of the fifth month of the Jiǎmǎo year of the Jiādìng era, the Master entered the monastery.
Pointing to the three gates, he said: "In this one gate of mine, there is absolutely no path for entry. How will you all proceed further?
Then, snapping his fingers once, he said: "Enter."
Entering the Buddha Hall, he said: "Who is it that is called 'Buddha'? And who is it that pays homage?
If you have not yet discerned the beginning and end of this matter, then look—this four-cornered floor has been laid bare to deceive all of you! Then he prostrated himself.

According to the Abbot, "In general, whoever occupies this seat must uphold this matter with the same rigor as the commands of Sun Wu or the laws of Shang Jun—there is death for violation, and no leniency.
Nevertheless, though it is thus, when the law is applied to its full extent, there are no subjects left."
Pointing to the Dharma seat, he said: "The true mandate is now being enacted; the ten directions are cut off at once. Paying homage to Mount Sumeru and King Lamp—what bowl are you seeking?
Having finished the prayers for the Emperor, he again took up incense and said: "All Buddhas of the three periods of time have exerted their full strength, yet they cannot lift it."
The ancestral masters of successive generations have a share in beholding this; yet the elder monks of all quarters have, to the end, failed to find its head or nose.
Only the Old Man Caoyuan of Donghu in Poyang, twenty years ago, managed to compare it with something else.

Unable to avoid bringing it forth before the assembly, he left it open for the people of the world to criticize and dissect as they please. He then took his seat. A monk asked: "An ancient said, 'For now, let us turn toward that which has not yet been met...'"
Having seen him, he stepped forward to receive him. "Is there still any room for you to act for others? The Master said, "There is no room for you to act for others.
He pressed further, saying, "Before the armor and helmet have even been donned, the thief’s body has already been exposed. The Master said, "Your failure, Senior, is all the more severe.
He pressed further, saying, "Before I have even asked or answered today, have I met with the Master? Is there mutual accord? The Master said, "Armor and helmet..."

Before he had even given [the gift], the thief’s true nature was already revealed. The Master advanced, saying, “A master of the school. The Teacher said, “Do not try to deceive people with empty talk.
The Master advanced again, saying, “How was it before you, Venerable, had seen Cao Yuan? The Teacher said, “Suining brought out his alms bowl. The Master advanced once more, saying—

[The student] asked, "What is it like after seeing? The Master said, "The mouth of the alms bowl points toward the sky. [The student] further asked, "What is it like when one has seen and when one has not yet seen?
The Master said, "Three people testify that a tortoise becomes a turtle. [The student] said, "I have caught and defeated this new old man! The Master said, [silently].
"Thieves! Thieves! As the monks prostrated, the Master suddenly took up his staff and showed it to the assembly, saying: "At the tip of this staff, the universe is empty;

throughout the ages, the traces of the thousand sages are nowhere to be found. Even if one knows the essential point before a word is raised, one is still separated by tens of thousands of layers of white clouds.
He then held the staff upright and said: "Look, look! This is the state prior to when the world had yet taken form and before sentient beings and Buddhas had yet been manifested."
"Breath. It is all right here. Upādyāya Chong has usually only sought to perfect himself alone; has he ever brought this forth?
Today, as the assembly of devas and humans gathers universally, having encountered this supreme mirror, it is impossible to escape.

I cannot help but reveal it directly before you, so that all people throughout the great earth may partake of it together. He then struck the ground once to the left and said, "If you can see it here—"

"Thoroughly penetrate! Seize the throats of the Buddhas and Patriarchs! He strikes once to the right and says, "If you see through here thoroughly, you will pierce the nostrils of all the monks under heaven.

Then, he strikes once in the middle and says, "If you see through here thoroughly, you will be worthy of repaying the unrequitable debt of gratitude and assisting in the transformation of non-action. At this very moment, tell me: what do you say?
"To whom does this merit belong? He then drew a line across his face and said: "The three borders are joyful to find all is well;

the four seas sing praises to celebrate peace. Again, he cited: When Luoshan entered the monastery and ascended the hall, as soon as he gathered his robes and was about to sit, he immediately said, "Take care!
After a long pause, he turned back and said, "Those who do not yet know, come forward! At that time, a monk just stepped out to pay his respects.
He bowed. Shanshan said, "It is truly bitter. The monk rose from his prostrations and said, "I, [Name], ask the Master. Luoshan then shouted and sent him out.

The Master said, "He cast his hook into the four seas only to catch a fierce dragon. Had the old man Luoshan, at that time, simply said 'Take care' and left it at that, he would have been somewhat better off.
But when he turned back and said, 'One who does not yet know—come forward,' he exposed his very heart and liver."

The internal organs have all been scrutinized and exposed by this monk. Nevertheless, though it is so: "The heavens are high and the herds of elephants are upright; the seas are vast and the hundred rivers flow toward them.
That evening, after the small *chan* (dharma) talk and the exchange of questions and answers were concluded, the Master said: "In the kingdom of Magadha," and then struck the meditation seat once.
The Master personally issued this command: "If you are a soaring falcon capable of piercing the clouds, you ought naturally to know the proper time.
Should you still linger to observe and listen, you, Venerable Chong, must not begrudge this single thread of your wretched life;

instead, cast open your three hundred and sixty joints and eighty-four thousand pores in their entirety and fling them into the midst of a bustling marketplace. [As for] the left eye, half a catty; the right..."
"Eight *liang* of eyes. On the starless scale of the patch-robed monk, he weighs the pounds and determines the ounces;
not a single point can deceive anyone. Thus one sees that Xinguang’s failure was no small matter. If this is not yet so, the opportune moment will be hard to encounter again.
Do not further deceive yourselves—once it has gone up, it is gone! He struck the meditation seat once and said, "Let us set this matter aside for now."
Again, it is recounted that Master Bao sent someone to deliver a message to Dayi (Sida), saying: "Why do you not go down the mountain to teach and transform sentient beings?
Why do you stare fixedly at the sky? Dayi replied: "The Buddhas of the three periods of time have all been swallowed by me in a single gulp;
where else are there any sentient beings left to be saved? The Master said: "Master Bao is teaching people to steal; this is no good."
The mind. Though their confessions were not yet fully extracted, the stolen goods had already been exposed.

Although these two great elders were renowned throughout the universe and held in high esteem by their contemporaries, when examined closely, [the Master] suddenly took up his staff, struck once, and said:
"In total, you do not yet know this one move."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The entire universe and the great earth do not contain so much as a single hair’s breadth.
Yet you all, slinging your staffs over your shoulders, travel on foot around the four worlds, saying, 'There is nowhere we have not reached; there is nothing we do not know. But tell me:
at the Nālandā Monastery in India today, what Dharma did the Master Śīlabhadra preach? He then descended from his seat.

Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the example of Fengxue addressing the assembly, saying: "If you establish even a single speck of dust, the state will flourish and the village elders will frown;
if you do not establish even a single speck of dust, the state will perish and the village elders will sing for joy. If you can understand this clearly, you have no share in it, O Ācārya."
It is entirely the old monk. If you do not understand this, the old monk is the *ācārya*.
Both the *ācārya* and the old monk can cause all people in the world to become deluded, and they can also cause all people in the world to attain awakening. Do you wish to recognize the *ācārya*?
(He strikes once to the left and says: "It is here. Do you wish to recognize the old monk? (He strikes once to the right and says: "It is here."

"Yes. The Master said: "The water used for ritual bowing and yielding still defiles the belly of an ox; how could the grain from amidst the drums and spears ever mix with the mouths of Yan Hui and Zhongni?
If you can see through the point where Guangxiao failed here, you will see that the Elder Fengxue has no master yet.
For now, let us set aside the single clap on the left; as for the single clap on the right, where does it land? No.
This is Zhang Hua’s eyes; he merely peers at the light of the shooting star. Descend from your seat.
Upon entering the hall: At the crossroads of the street, there is a living path, yet those of immeasurable capacity do not know where it leads.
Having no place to land, if you intend to follow in its tracks, [you must look] to the Western Heaven and this land.

Ascending the hall, he said: "Sentient beings are hindered by their own understanding; Bodhisattvas have not yet transcended conceptualization. He suddenly called out to the assembly, "Do you understand?
Narrowness and lack of reverence—gentlemen do not follow such paths."
Ascending the hall, he said: "When one reaches an impasse, there must be change; when there is change, there is penetration.

To take the lantern and place it inside the Buddha Hall, and to take the main gate and place it upon the lantern—this is something people know exists. Yet, as for Mañjuśrī, the teacher of the seven Buddhas, why was he unable to emerge from the woman’s samādhi?"
Ascending the hall for the Mid-Autumn Festival, he suddenly took up his staff and said, "Today is the Mid-Autumn Festival; the staff is most urgent in its service to people.
He drew a line and said, "Pushing aside the clouds over a thousand peaks. He struck a circle and said, "Releasing a single orb of the moon.
"If you can realize it before the light has even arisen, you will still have added a layer of dust to your eyes. Leaning on his staff, he descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the following case: Attendant Kuò asked Dēngshān, "Where have all the sages of the past gone? Dēngshān said, "What? What?
Kuò said, "When the imperial decree summons the flying dragon horse, the lame tortoise sticks its head out. Dēngshān then desisted.
The next day, after bathing, as Kuò was passing tea to him, Dēngshān patted Kuò on the back and said, "How about yesterday’s case? Kuò—
[The Master] said, "This old fellow! Only today has he finally found his footing. The Teacher said, "To comb a tiger’s whiskers and pull at a tiger’s tail—this monk certainly did so;
he nearly escaped not from the tiger’s mouth. Although Old Deshan was utterly acting like a fool, he could not deceive Guangxiao’s eyes."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The entire great earth is the original face of all of you. Why is it that the eyes do not see the nostrils?
Even if one were exceptionally clear-sighted, one would still not avoid mistaking the bridge of a donkey’s saddle for one’s father’s chin.
Furthermore, before the world was established and before parents were born, how could one communicate this? After a long silence, he said: 'In my youth, I once made a decisive resolution.'"
The Dragon-Snake Array. Old and decrepit, too weary to listen to the songs of children.

[Addressing] the Head Seat, the Librarian, and the Rector as they enter the hall: Before the wooden mallet has even struck, the entire Great Canon of the Teachings is vividly manifest in its characters and meanings;
the Buddhas of the three periods have their mouths hung upon the wall. At such a time as this, tell me: who is it?
The family style of wind and moon; the eyes and mind of humans and devas; the model for all time past and present.
[He] then descended from his seat. Entering the hall: "All that has form is entirely illusory. In Huaizhou, the ox eats the grain; in Yizhou, the horse’s belly swells."
"If one sees that all marks are non-marks, then one sees the Tathāgata.
[He] took up his whisk and called to the assembly, saying, "The Old Śākyamuni has arrived! Do you see him? After a long silence, he said, "Go to the hall to drink tea."
Ascending the hall, he cited the verse of Master Bodhidharma: "I have come to this land / To transmit the Dharma and save deluded beings.

/ One flower opens into five petals; / The fruiting of the result is accomplished naturally. The Master said: "Those who use heterodox ways to delude the people shall certainly be executed without pardon."
Nevertheless, even so: were it not for Liuyi’s transmission of the letter, how could one have seen the profound palaces of the Dragon King?

As he ascended the hall during a long period of rain, he took up his staff, drew a circle, and addressed the assembly, saying: "Do you see it? He then declared: "The blazing sun is in the midst of the sky.
Throwing down the staff, he said: "All darkness naturally submits. He then descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised up an instance from Fayen, who said to the assembly: "Throughout the entire world of the ten directions, all is bright and clear;

there is not a single thread of hair. If there were a single thread of hair, it would indeed be a single thread of hair. The Master said: "To have traveled through the six kingdoms is not yet a sound strategy."
To starve to death on Mount Shouyang—how could that be considered a brilliant strategy? The ancient masters’ way of life as ghosts has been fully exposed for you all.
Do you know where Guangxiao Temple stands? After a long silence, he said: "The roots of the ancient locust tree emerge from the county; when the official is pure, the horse’s bones stand high."
When Head Seat Yuan went up to the hall for the formal lecture, [the Master said]: "One must not face it; one must not turn one's back to it.
If even a hair’s breadth remains unexhausted, the ancient mirror will develop flaws. He suddenly took up his staff, saying: "Lifting this iron caltrop," and striking once, he said:
"All at once they are smashed to pieces. Throwing down the staff, he said: "Let the great earth be left in a vast, dark expanse; the ancients had their own way of penetrating through."

The Master enters the hall. "If you understand, then all things are of one family. He strikes the meditation seat once and says, "Tell me, beyond the Floating Banner King Land, is there still this news or not?
If you do not understand, then there are ten thousand distinctions and a thousand differences. For us monks..."
When walking, simply walk; when sitting, simply sit. Even with ten thousand distinctions and a thousand variations, what fault is there?
After a long silence, he said: "Study! He ascended the hall and said: "The entire earth is your own self. Where would you place the grasses, weeds, humans, and animals?
Even if you can see through this with total penetration, it is merely making a living inside a rat's hole. He struck the meditation seat once to the left.
Yun said: "Take it and place it over here. As for the Bodhisattva Sadāprarudita, who sold his heart and liver—after all, whom did he intend to teach the Prajñāpāramitā?
After a long silence, he said: "The offense shall not be judged too severely."

Ascending the hall, he said: "When a person of integrity speaks of deviant teachings, those deviant teachings are entirely correct. When a deviant person speaks of orthodox teachings, those orthodox teachings are entirely deviant.
He suddenly called out to the assembly, saying: "Rather than praising Yao and disparaging Jie, why not forget both and transform into the Dao?
Although this is so, people of this age will surely laugh at me; those who can truly laugh are rare indeed.

Ascending the hall for the Imperial Birthday: On this auspicious occasion of the Imperial Birthday, I cannot help but lecture once upon the *Sūtra on the King Protecting the State* to offer prayers for the Emperor’s long life.
Then, raising his whisk, he calls to the assembly, saying: "To explain this sūtra, there are two main divisions.
Striking the left side of the meditation seat with the whisk, he says: "First, the explanation of the title. Striking once on the right side, he says: "Second, the commentary on the text."
The Main Text: Using the whisk, he makes a single dot in the center and says: "Within this Main Text, it is divided into three parts. What are these three?
He drops the whisk, stands with hands joined in *añjali*, and cries: "Ten thousand years! Ten thousand years! Ten thousand times ten thousand years!"
Ascending the hall, he said: "The superior person, with a single resolution, brings everything to an end. As for those who wander about like wild hunters, what limit is there to them?

When those of middle and lower capacity hear this, they mostly do not believe it. Even if one were to travel around the four continents searching for a single person who does not believe, there would truly be none among ten thousand.
Why is this? For pure tea and simple talk, it is hard to find a friend; for turbid wine and wild songs, it is easy to find companions."
The Recorded Sayings of the Jiankang Prefecture Jangshan Taiping Xingguo Chan Monastery,
compiled by the Dharma-heir disciples residing at the Jiankang Prefecture Qingliangshan Guanghui Chan Monastery, including (Wukai), and others.
He points to the three gates and burns incense, addressing the great assembly: "To enter these gates, there is from the outset no expedient means;
it requires that each of you possess the eye upon the tip of your toe. If this is not yet the case, then as a guest, your sentiments will follow after others at every step."
Entering the Buddha Hall, he pointed at the Buddha with his incense burner and said, "The ancient Śākyamuni was not first. Then, pointing at himself, he said, "The present Maitreya is not last.
Thereupon, burning incense, he said: "A single thread connects the prostrations and the burning of incense; let it be taught so as to break open the mouths of the monks."

The Abbot sat upon his seat, looked over the assembly, and said: "In the kingdom of Magadha, he personally issued this command, causing all people throughout the great earth to lose their bodies and forfeit their lives.
Now tell me, does the new Jingshan still have eyebrows? He gave a shout and rose.

Pointing to the Dharma seat, he said: "Severing the summit of Vairocana, trampling the paths of a thousand differences—Mount Sumeru and King of Lamps have no place for my feet to rest. Thereupon, he strode up to the seat;

after offering incense and making prayers for the Emperor, he adjusted his robes and sat down. A monk asked: "I recall Xinghua’s opening of the hall, where he addressed the assembly, saying: 'This one...'"

"A single incense offering is originally for the Three Sages; yet the Three Sages are too solitary for me. What is the underlying meaning? The Master said, "The confession comes from the mouth of the prisoner.
The student pressed further, "I simply wish to inherit the lineage of Dayue; yet Dayue is too distant for me. How then shall it be?"
The Master said, "A second offense will not be tolerated. The student stepped forward and asked, "Later it was said:

'If you had not been struck by Dajue, how would we have seen the news of Linji eating blows at Huangbo? What does this mean? The Master said, "Your failure is even more profound. The student stepped forward and asked, "..."
“Just as it was when Linji was with Huangbo, what did he obtain there? The Master said, “He stepped on a scale-weight; it was harder than iron.
The student asked, “Since he received blows at the hands of Dayue, for what reason did he succeed Linji? The Master said, “Only by knowing gratitude can one understand how to repay it.
The student asked, “I wonder whose song the Master sings? Whose ancestral style does his lineage follow? The Master—
[The Master] said, "Elder, are you deaf? Xuefeng advanced and said, "The Master has attained the power of Old Man De; you have attained the power of Caoshan.
The Master said, "Let the people of the world criticize you as they will. Xuefeng said, "Were it not for the wild geese arriving last night, how could one see the autumn at the sea gate?"
The Master said, "Thief! Thief! The monk stepped forward and said, "A master of the school.
He then prostrated. The Master then said: "The staff and flask were once lodged here; mountain clouds drifted and waters flowed.
Now, returning again to this place of practice, the assembly of water and clouds remains as solemn as ever. I recall being here twenty years ago. From...
At the dwelling of the Great Being Bao Gong, I obtained a most extraordinary karmic connection. On a vast scale, it encompasses the ocean of worlds without interval;
on a minute scale, it enters the space between atoms without omission. To dwell in peace with the times and accord with circumstances, one gazes upon the heavens and feels naturally content.
To respond to others and engage with things, to manage affairs and regulate changes, one possesses abundant ease and surplus capacity. At that time, I understood this principle.
It cannot be attained. Even now, though I have understood it, I intended to reveal a small portion of it to meet the demands of the occasion.
Yet, as soon as I entered the gate, I was confounded by the bells, fish-shaped gongs, drums, and wooden clappers; suddenly, I could find no point of entry.
Even with a strategy that pierces the heavens, there is nowhere to deploy it. Nevertheless, who says there is no one to appraise the Bian-king jade? I—
"The Way is like a black pearl; wherever it goes, it shines. Again, he raised the case:
Xinghua addressed the assembly, saying, "When I meet people, I bring it forth; when I bring it forth, it is not for the sake of others. Sansheng said: [It is]...
"When I meet someone, I do not come forth; when I come forth, I am already a person. Later, Master Zhenneng said, "Look at these two old fellows;
they have stolen a mere fraction of Linji’s livelihood and each has demarcated their own territory and boundaries.
To an eye of clear vision, this is nothing but a laughable matter. The Master said, "Zhenneng’s critique like this only knows one side of the matter; he does not know the other."
To know these two [cases] is already enough to make even a clear-eyed monk only smile with derision.
What they do not realize is that these two great elders joined hands to destroy the true lineage of Linji; it is not worth a single coin. Now tell me:
does New Zhongshan’s critique in this manner avoid the laughter of clear-eyed monks? Please try to discern this for yourself.
That evening, during the informal lecture (xiaochan), a monk asked: "To obtain the treasures of the Jewel Mountain, one must pass through Yuanwu’s barrier.

I know this is a matter within the domain of a patch-robed monk; why is it that out of ten, five pairs fail to pass through here? The Master said, "It is actually quite close. The monk pressed further:
"To pass the barrier, one must have the eye to pass the barrier; to obtain the treasure, one must rely on a person who can discern the treasure. The Master [replied].
[The Master] said, "Just right for a blow of the staff. The student asked, "What is the barrier of Yuanwu? The Master said, "All the people in the entire world cannot pass through it.
The student asked, "What are the treasures of the Jewel Mountain? The Master said, "A single blow of the hammer has shattered them all. The student asked, "..."
"Today’s assembly consists entirely of those who have passed through the barrier; they have already obtained the treasure from the Jewel Mountain.
But tell me, does the Master approve? The Master said, "In thirty years, I have rarely encountered such as these.

The monk pressed further, "If one lacks such an eye for selecting Buddhas, what would even a thousand years of practice avail? The Master said, "How many people can truly know this mind? The monk bowed.
The Master then said: "Yuanwu’s single barrier is the most perilous in the world; the treasure on the Jewel Mountain is rare in all ages.
To penetrate the barrier and find the treasure—this still falls into my second-grade teaching. Therefore it is said: 'To penetrate the barrier, one must possess the eye for penetrating the barrier;

to obtain the treasure, one must be a person who recognizes the treasure. Only when one possesses the eye for penetrating the barrier and is a person who can distinguish the treasure can they begin to penetrate Yuanwu."
Upon awakening at the barrier, one attains the treasures of the Jewel Mountain and is thus able to emerge from all perils and difficulties and pass beyond all confusions and contradictions.
One may then use one's own treasury to relieve the orphaned and the poor, never again selling off pearls for the price of peas.
Although this is so, what if, suddenly, one were toppled over the Barrier of Yuanwu by Jiangshan and the treasures of the Jewel Mountain were shattered? At such a time—

At such a time, even if all people were to possess the eye that penetrates the barrier and were entirely connoisseurs of jewels, upon reaching this point, not a single skillful means would be of any use.
Why? Because "The momentum of a thousand peaks ceases at the foot of the mountain; the sound of ten thousand streams vanishes upon reaching the sea."
Again, Master Faden addressed the assembly, saying: "I originally intended to hide deep within mountain caves and remain in seclusion until my time passed away.
However, because the Elder Qingliang has a case that remains unresolved, I cannot help but come forth to settle it for him.
A monk stepped forward and asked, "I do not know, Master, what unresolved case the Elder Qingliang has? Faden raised his staff.

Dafu said, "The patriarchs and ancestors could not resolve it; the calamity has now reached their descendants. The monk asked, "Where does the fault lie? Dafu said, "The fault lies with me; the calamity reaches you.
The Master [Zhaozhou] said, "Generally speaking, when those of the ancestral school emerge from seclusion, there is nothing they do not resolve.
Look at that Fadelong: for the sake of Qingjing, he brought this unresolved case to a direct conclusion across three lifetimes."
"Sixty kalpas. The late Master Chong’s original intent was likewise so.

It is because the Old Man of Cao Yuan has a kōan that remains unresolved that [the Master] could not help but come forth to settle it for him. When a monk comes out, he immediately returns to his quarters.
If you should suddenly say, "Three lives, sixty kalpas," simply respond to him by saying, "I grant you one eye."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "When it manifests, it takes form. He suddenly took up his staff and said, "This very thing here is the staff.
When it is quiescent, it is dark and hidden. Holding the staff upright, he called to the assembly, saying, "Look! Look! It pierces through your nostrils and replaces your eyes.
Thirty years from now, when you have attained awakening, you will finally know that the function of this staff was not applied in vain. He leaned on the staff and descended.

Seated. Ascending the hall to celebrate the auspicious occasion of the Emperor’s birthday. The Imperial Son-in-law (the Crown Prince) inquires after his well-being, reverently providing for him with the care of gathering *lan* flowers.

As the month of *Rui-bin* (*Wu-hsi*) marks this season, the time when auspicious signs are nurtured and gathered, the vast earth shines with glory and the hearts of all rejoice. Thus it is said: "Rolling forth the thunder of the Dharma."

Beating the Dharma drum, spreading the clouds of compassion, and sprinkling the nectar of immortality—taking this very Dharma as the total transmission, I vow to be the mother of all Buddhas in every generation.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "Mind, Buddha, and sentient beings—these three are without distinction. What is the past mind?"
The Master said, "Let it go; wait until it has cooled, then come look. The student asked, "What is the present mind?
The Master said, "You ask and I answer. The student asked, "What is the future mind? The Master said, "I will tell you when I ascend the hall next time. The student said, "..."
"What is the Buddha of the past? The Master said, "Last year’s plum blossoms. The student asked, "What is the Buddha of the present?
The Master said, "This year’s willows. The student asked, "What is the Buddha of the future? The Master said, "Their color and fragrance remain as they were."
Jin asked, "What is the wisdom of differentiation regarding the past? He then struck the left side of the meditation seat with his whisk.
Jin asked, "What is the wisdom of differentiation regarding the present? He again struck the right side of the meditation seat with his whisk. Jin asked, [and so forth].
"What is the wisdom that distinguishes the future? The Master took his whisk and made a single dot in the middle.
The monk stepped forward and said, "The mind, the Buddha, and sentient beings have no turning away from one another; the ocean of lands in the ten directions is gathered within a single hair.
