A person transmitted [the following]: "It is simply not something else that is inherently possessed. The Master said, "Since it is not something else that is inherently possessed, tell me, what is it that he constantly makes use of?
Shan said, "Just so, just so. The Master said, "You have deceived an entire boatload of people! The Master then called to the assembly, saying, "It is so, it is so.
The qilin and auspicious phoenix are not rare treasures for adorning the world; the sound of gold when cast upon the ground is what is noble."

This is not something to be treasured. Under the school of Caoshan, one has more than enough to behold; yet under the school of the patch-robed monks, one must still buy straw sandals and travel on foot before one can attain it.
He ascended the hall and said: "The Great Master Bodhidharma sat there at Shaolin, huddled and cold for nine years. This was truly enough to make people..."
They harbor doubts and attachments. Yet, when it came to explaining the method for settling the mind to the Second Patriarch, the very life-force of all beings fell into the hands of the world;
to this day, no one has been able to inspect it thoroughly. Nevertheless, once bitten by a snake, one fears even the sight of a broken well-rope.
He invited Master Jingzhong to serve as the Head Seat. Ascending the hall, he raised the case of Chan Master Huangbo, who served as the Head Seat in Nanquan’s assembly.
One day, while holding his alms bowl, he sat in Nanquan’s seat. When Nanquan entered the hall and saw him, he asked:
The Elder was practicing the Way for many years. Huangbo said, "Before King Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja.
Yuanquan said, "That is still the descendant of Old Master Wang; go down [from the seat]. Huangbo then took up his alms bowl and sat in the second position. Yuanquan desisted. The Master said:
"Huangbo was like Guan Yu, who charged straight into an array of a million troops and alone took the head of Yan Liang. His...
Nanquan possessed the strategic foresight to encompass all heroes under heaven; without moving a blade or a shield, he brought about a reign of peace.
Jiangshan Mountain precisely requires such a person to sit upon the seat of the Dharma bowl. Having descended from the seat, together with the great assembly, we reverently entreat him.
Ascending the hall: "Mount Sumeru may be split asunder; the waters of the great ocean may be exhausted. Yet, when it comes to this matter, one would rather cut out one's tongue.
Ascending the hall: [The Master] raised the following case: When Mingzhao arrived at Zhaoqing, there was an elder named Du who asked him:

"Luoshan used to say constantly, 'In all other quarters, there is only millet porridge; only at Luoshan is there a single flavor of white rice. Brother, having come from Luoshan, why do you now [act otherwise]?"
Handan said, "I have been invited to some white rice. Mingzhao clapped his hands twice. Handan said, "I thought it was white rice;
it turns out it is only *māṣa*-flour porridge. Mingzhao said, "Foolish man! A staff could not kill you even if struck.
That night, Handan recounted this to several Zen guests. Mingzhao approached him and said, "How do you do? Handan said, "Today is indeed this very thing."
As he was lowering his two palms, the senior monk Tao said, "There is no need to lower your palms;
how would you speak from within? Mingzhao said, "Speak, speak from within! Tao had no reply. Mingzhao said, "This is for all of you."
At one time, he bound them all together into a single bundle, stood it upside down facing his urinal, and said, "See you tomorrow; take care.
Master Yunmen remarked: "Although Mingzhao was like a skilled warrior who destroys cities and towns—crushing whatever he encounters and subduing whatever he meets—"
If one examines this from the perspective of the future, it cannot be avoided that he was overly ostentatious in his brilliance and thus fell short in the dark.
At that time, had the two senior monks, Du and Tao, been skillful in responding to the immediate situation, Mingzhao would have ended up falling flat on his face in a puddle of urine. Now tell me:
did they approve of Mingzhao, or did they not?
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: Xuefeng knocked on the door of Old Master Guan. Guan asked, "Who is it? Xuefeng said, "A phoenix chick. Guan asked, "What are you doing here?
Xuefeng said, "To scoop up Old Guan! Guan then opened the door; just as Xuefeng was about to enter, Guan grabbed him and said, "Speak!
Speak! Xuefeng hesitated, and Guan pushed him out. The Master said, "Everywhere people say that Old Guan’s gate and walls—"
It stands like a sheer cliff. Little do you realize that even before the gate was opened, it had already been swallowed by Xuefeng.
Why, then, did he say, "If I had entered the gate of Old Guan at that time, where would you lot—this crew of wine-dregs eaters—go to grope for it?
The Master said, "They are equally acting foolishly and peddling their eccentricities; yet among them, there is a slight difference. There was an old man...
The Old Master said: "Xuefeng had these words, but at that time he could not enter; even now he still cannot enter. The Teacher said:
"If it were not for this old master who deeply discerned the subtle nuances, how could one see that Xuefeng’s merit was as great as that of a horse-sweating general?
Xuedou said: "This ungrateful wretch—what connection does he have? That he could not enter at that time, how could it be considered [a failure]?"
"You entered. Now that you have searched for it and failed to find it, you have caused Xuefeng to suffer in vain. Both were under the gate of Old Guan.
The Master said, "Although Xuedou has exerted his full strength to uphold Xuefeng, he cannot avoid having missed the mark regarding the old master."
Ascending the hall: The abbot’s quarters have been damaged; there is no place for rest. The monastery lacks provisions; the community cannot be supported.
Old debts accumulate like the sea; there is no money to repay them. The Great Way is right before one's eyes; though one has a mouth, it cannot speak of it.
If a person can penetrate these four gates, they are fit to serve as a model for all quarters. Zhaozhou personally saw the old Nanquan. Observe!
In the Sound Hall, there was Maitreya.
He ascended the hall and cited Dongshan’s instruction to the assembly, saying: "Right here, one must ensure that every phrase is uninterrupted before it will do.
It is like the main thoroughfares of Chang'an, where news and travelers never cease; if even a single road were blocked, it would mean one is no longer in service."
"Regarding Your Majesty: this man’s life hangs by a thread. The Master said: "Li Ling was captured alive in the barbarian court;
Su Wu grazed sheep on the shores of the sea. Is this serving Your Majesty, or not? On the roads of Chang’an, is news communicated, or is it not?
If one can discern this, one may naturally become the master wherever one is and bring about a state of Great Peace. If it is otherwise, [one’s] life..."
Like a dangling thread.
Entering the hall, [the Master said]: "To have awakened to the Way upon hearing bamboo strike—clearly, one does not understand the Zen of the Patriarchs.

To see peach blossoms and feel no doubt—I dare say you, elder brother, have still not reached the bottom. For the most part, even if true gold has been refined a hundred times, it must still pass through the hammer and tongs of the fundamental division."

Today at Jiangshan, one stands before the furnace unflinching as sparks fly; I dare say that Yangshan and Xuansha have never even dreamed of this, while Xiangyan and Lingyun are still reeking of the stench of sweat.

Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the case of Jia Shan and Ding Shan traveling together. Ding Shan said, "In birth-and-death there is no Buddha; if there were a Buddha, there would be no birth-and-death.
The Master said, "A black ox lies dead in stagnant water. Jia Shan said, "Within birth-and-death there is a Buddha; thus one does not become deluded by birth-and-death.
The Master said, "A mangy horse is tied to a withered post. The two men could not agree with one another and went together to visit Damei. Jia...
Shanshan asked, "I do not know which one is intimate and which one is distant. The Master said, "One carves one's own belly oneself;
do not listen to others wielding fishing rods. Damei said, "One is intimate, one is distant.
The Master said, "A master of the school possesses natural authority. Jiashan said, "I wonder, which one is intimate? The Master said, "This fellow is still nodding off."
He was still not awake. Daimei said, "Go for now and come back tomorrow. The Master said, "If he does not turn his head when called, what can be done?

The next day, Jiashan came to the abbot’s quarters and asked again. The Master said, "As expected, you were still talking in your sleep. Daimei said, "Those who are close do not ask; those who ask are not close.
The Master said, "To kill a person, no knife is needed; to bring a person to life, no sword is required. Jiashan—[realized].
After he was admitted to the monastery, he said, "When I was first at Damei, I lost one of my eyes. The Master said, "A poor man thinks of his old debts.
He then called to the assembly, saying, "Do you all know where the old man of Damei has ended up?"
After a long silence, he said: "To distinguish dragons from snakes, how must the eye be upright? To seize tigers and rhinoceroses, one's timing must not be incomplete.
Ascending the hall, he saw a small object standing before him. He then held up his staff and said: "Tell me, is this an object or not an object?
If you say it is the nature of consciousness (*vijñapti-mātratā*), you must strictly avoid calling this 'the staff,' for that implies a state of attainment."
Therefore, it is not called "the staff. What would you call it? It is not a real abiding in consciousness-only; to dwell in attachment is an error.
He suddenly addressed the assembly, saying: "Even if one were to strip away layer upon layer until nothing remains," and then he struck the ground once with the staff, saying:
"The Vajra-jewel sword does not spare him!"
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the case of National Teacher Yanguan. One day, he called to his attendant and said, "Bring me my rhinoceros-horn fan.

The attendant said, "Although it is but a humble household utensil, it is nonetheless indispensable. The National Teacher said, "The fan is broken. The attendant said, "If it were not broken, what would it be good for? The National Teacher said, "Give me back the rhinoceros! [The Master] said: "Though it is but a common household item, it is indeed something that cannot be dispensed with. When the attendant said, 'The fan is broken,' the National Teacher asked, 'If it were not broken, what would it be good for?

Finally, he said, 'Give me back the rhinoceros! This was the National Teacher’s way of testing the attendant; it was not merely a matter of a fan. If you can see this point, you will understand the meaning of the National Teacher’s words. If you cannot, you must look further. He then chanted: "The fan is broken, yet the rhinoceros is still there; The rhinoceros is returned, yet the fan remains. He then descended from the seat.
The Master said, "A poor child thinks of an old debt. The attendant was speechless. The Master said, "Had it not been for this attendant, I might have answered incorrectly.
Touzi said, "I would not have refused to bring it forth, but I feared the horns would not be complete.
The Master said, "Touzi wanted to give the attendant a living eye, yet he missed the mark with the attendant. Xuedou said, "I want them incomplete."
“Bottom, head, and horns. The Master said, “Great as Xuedou may be, he could not leap out of the attendant’s trap.
Shishuang said, “If it were you, Reverend, there would be none at all. The Master said, “The tail has already been exposed. Xuedou said, “The rhinoceros calf is still here.”
The Master said, "Alas, its horns are incomplete. Zifu drew a circle and wrote the character for "ox" (牛) in the center.
The Master said, "From the very beginning, there was no need to bring this out. Xuedou said, "Why did you not bring it out earlier?
The Master said, "The matter remains. Baofu said, "The Master is advanced in years; it would be better to ask someone else. The Master said, "I only fear it will be difficult for them."
"Another person. Xuedou said, "What a pity; labor spent without merit. The Master said, "It is not beyond one's capacity.

The Master suddenly called out to the assembly, "This group of old men—if they had personally attained the use of the rhinoceros-horn fan, they would never have been so exhausted, parched, and clamoring. Have you all ever attained such use? Each of you, please..."
Return to the hall. Inspect the preparations. Ascend the hall.
The Master cites the case of Monk Micang. A monk came to pay his respects; he circumambulated the meditation seat three times and struck it, saying:
The monk said, "I do not see the master; I shall no longer go to the hall. Miyun asked, "Where have your conceptual consciousnesses gone?
The monk said, "Indeed, they are not here. Miyun struck him. The monk said, "I nearly fell into conceptual consciousness! and laughed loudly.
Miyun said, "At the edge of the village path, you encounter someone; what words could there possibly be? The monk went to the hall. The Master said, "This monk is habituated..."

In the midst of the battle array, their advances, retreats, sittings, and movements did not fail to maintain their propriety; yet they rolled themselves into the "Confusing the Soul" camp, where they had no way to turn back.

While Mi Cang assessed the enemy's strength—both its reality and its pretense—and displayed his skill in seizing and relinquishing positions, he was nonetheless unable to destroy their nest or capture their kindred.
Consequently, the enemy’s arrogance grew even greater. Had they been in Jiangshan’s hands, moreover...
"How shall we manage this? He struck the meditation seat once and said, "Study! Then he descended from the seat.
Upon ascending the hall, after completing his introductory remarks, he called to the attendant, "What did I just say?
As the attendant was about to respond, he said, "The assembly, take this clearly to heart; present it to those who are masters. He then descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the case of Master Gaoting, who went to visit Deshan. Seeing Deshan sitting on the riverbank from across the water, Gaoting greeted him from across the river.
Deshan beckoned him with his hand, and Gaoting was suddenly enlightened; he then strode straight across and did not cross the river at all. The Master said:
"Deshan possesses the poison of a 'sand-swallowing' [shark] that shoots its prey; Gaoting took one dose of it."
He will not live again.
[The Master] ascends the hall and cites Chan Master Yongming Shou. Because two monks came to seek instruction, he asked the head monk, "Have you been here before?
The monk replied, "I have. He then asked the second seat, "Have you been here before? The monk...
[The monk] said, "I have never been there. Yongming said, "One has gained, one has lost.
After a short while, the attendant asked, "Regarding those two monks just now, I do not know which one gained and which one lost. Yongming said, "Did you ever know these two monks?
The attendant said, "I did not know them. Yongming said, "In the same pit, there is no different soil. The Master said, "Whether arriving or not arriving, it is one gain."
One mistake: it was neither arsenic nor rock honey. With no eyes upon the tip of the tongue, how can one eat?
Just as the attendant was about to inquire for the truth, do not blame those in the same pit for having different soil; before the lightning has subsided, the thunderclap roars.

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The Treasury of the True Dharma Eye has been handed down from generation to generation since the time of the mistaken transmission at Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa to Kāśyapa.
Thus, they have followed the error with the error. Yet, the sword that strikes the great bell does not merely slice the meat upon the cutting board; if one skillfully wields its handle,"
Thus, the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye has been entrusted to its rightful place.
He ascended the hall, took up his staff, and called to the assembly, saying, "Do you see it? He then held the staff upright and said, "Upright, it exhausts the three periods of time."
Holding his staff horizontally, he said: "It stretches across the ten directions. He struck once and said: "A thousand words and ten thousand phrases—no one understands them.
He threw down the staff and said: "Furthermore, it follows the warbling oriole over the low wall."
When Yuan the Head Seat ascended the hall for the formal sermon, he recounted the case of Head Seat Xianying, who had visited Ciming.
Ciming asked, "Where have you recently departed from? Ying replied, "Jinluan. Ciming asked, "Where did you spend the summer retreat? Ying replied, "Jinluan. Ciming asked, "Where were you last summer?
Ying replied, "Jinluan. Ciming asked, "Where were you the previous summer? Ying replied, "Jinluan. Ciming asked, "Where were you before that? Ying replied, "Jinluan. Ciming said, "First—"
"Where were you last summer? Ying said. "Master, why do you not lead me through the meaning of this? Ming said, "I also cannot examine you;
I shall have the son from the storehouse come to examine you. For now, serve a bowl of tea to moisten your mouth."
The Master said: "Although Ciming’s noble household was as deep as the sea, he did not refuse those who came.
Ying, it is true that the traveler's road is as vast as heaven and one passes through it without leaving a trace. But consider this: when Ciming said, 'I have not yet examined you;
let me first serve you a bowl of tea to moisten your mouth,' what was his intention? When meeting a swordsman on the road, one must present oneself."
Sword. It is not that the poet did not offer his poem; he simply did not.
Entering the hall, the Master raised the example of Mazu Daoshi, who said: "Arhats hear and see the Buddha-nature; Bodhisattvas see the Buddha-nature with their eyes.
To realize them as non-dual is called the nature of equality. The Master said: "Jiangshan will cast a single eye to accord with Mazu Daoshi."
We have seen one another and now depart. The celestial deities return to heaven; the terrestrial deities return to earth; the coins return to the treasury; the horses return to their stalls.
Gazing up at the void, I humbly entreat you to take care of yourselves. Thereupon, he descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall to discourse on the method of walking the fields: "A stretch of idle land before the mountain. The Master said, "When an object meets its master, the eye stands firm.
"With hands folded, he earnestly questions his ancestral father. The Master said, "It is one's own original nature. "Where is the deed? "How many times has it been sold, only to be bought back again?
The Master said, "After the sound of the chime has ceased, you must not regret it. "Out of pity for the pines and bamboos, he leads them [in]."
"Pure Wind. The Master said, "The wind moves the gentleman. The flaws in Dongshan have already been exposed by Jiangshan.
But tell me, is there anyone who can point out the flaws in Jiangshan? After a long silence, he said, "Our Emperor has issued an imperial decree."
A general amnesty was proclaimed and all were released.
He ascended the hall and cited Huitang’s words to Yuanwu: "Brother Qin, how have you been lately? Yuanwu replied, "Arising and ceasing without stopping.
Huitang said, "One can see what an ordinary person of this world is like. Twenty years ago, I too used to come here in such a state."
"And now, at this assembly, even from the tip of his foot, he kicks out a Buddha. The Master said:
"How could an ordinary person of the mundane world, whose arising and ceasing are never still, be able to kick out a Buddha from the tip of his foot?

Only when one truly kicks out a Buddha from the tip of one's foot is one such an ordinary person of the mundane world whose arising and ceasing are never still. This is the spiritual power of the ground."
At every step, there is the grass of the Snowy Mountains; every monk is a pearl from the sea of the Cāṇūra Ocean. Entering the hall, he said:
"The meaning of Huangmei cannot be grasped by those who understand the Dharma. Linji’s True Eye was extinguished by this blind donkey.
These two points alone bring calamity upon the monks of the world: they seek life but cannot find it; they seek death but cannot find it."
He passed away. Reflecting on this, I think of the old Chan master Tiezui, who could say, "The former master did not speak these words.
He ascended the hall and said: A monk asked Shitou, "What is Chan? Shitou replied, "A paving brick. "What is the Way? Shitou replied, "A wooden post. The Master said:
"Clear water and plain soup—few can know their true flavor. Among gourds, earth, leather, and wood, those who truly understand them are rare."
Sound. Ascending the hall: "The dragon roars from a withered tree; all sounds are utterly extinguished. The eye in a skull is alive;
all forms and appearances are empty. To look at it is to go blind; to listen to it is to go deaf. How laughable that the Great Being Avalokiteśvara should have attained realization for no reason!"
Yuantong, having thanked the lay practitioner for his departure, ascended the hall and said: "A monk took his leave of Da-sui. Da-sui asked, 'Where are you going?
The monk replied, 'I am going down the mountain to teach and transform others. Da-sui said, 'The entire earth is my patron (dānapati). Where will you go to seek alms? The monk said, 'Right there.'"
[The Master] asked for the head of the discourse. Da Sui said, "You have not yet gone. The Master said, "Da Sui has the hand of an eagle-shooter; his arrows are never shot in vain.
This monk possesses the mechanism of biting the arrowhead; he bit and held fast upon meeting the point of the shaft.
For what reason did Da Sui nevertheless say, 'You have not yet gone'? After a long silence, he said, "If true gold does not pass through the furnace and bellows, how can it attain its brilliance?"
Thoroughly Fresh. Ascending the hall, he raised a case: A monk was taking his leave of Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou asked, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "To Xuefeng.
Zhaozhou said, "If they ask the Master what words or phrases you have [for them], how will you answer? The monk said, "I shall instead request the Master [to speak for me]."
The Master said, "Although this monk is skilled at turning the spearhead around, he cannot avoid having his blade dull.
Zhaozhou said, "In winter one speaks of cold; in summer one speaks of heat. He then asked the monk, "If someone were to suddenly ask you about the ultimate matter, what would you say?
The monk was speechless. Zhaozhou said, "Just say that you have come to Zhaozhou in person; you are no mere messenger. The Master said, "Everyone says it is Zhaozhou..."
Zhaozhou presented his case before this monk, little realizing that within it lay a scheme to swallow up all the heroes under heaven.
Later, the monk went to Xuefeng. Xuefeng asked, “Where have you come from? The monk replied, “From Zhaozhou. Xuefeng asked, “What words were spoken there?
The monk recounted the previous conversation. The Master [Xuefeng] said, “Even transmitting words and conveying messages has not yet been achieved. Xuefeng continued, “It must...”
This was only achieved by Zhaozhou. The Master said, "Sweet in the mouth but bitter in the heart; such a person is loathed.

He then called to the assembly, saying, "At that time, had this monk possessed the eye of prior knowledge before the words were even raised, those two great elders would have had to beg for their lives from his hands.
Nevertheless, though it is so, Zhaozhou’s barrier is perilous and difficult for people to penetrate; Xueqiao’s peak is high and the path is impassable."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "A great practitioner of the Way is captured by demons; a person of great icchantika-nature is sustained by the Buddha.
If one is not sustained by the Buddha, they are insufficient to be a demon; if one is not captured by a demon, they are insufficient to be a Buddha.

Thus, the demon is the very substance of the Buddha, and the Buddha is the function of the demon. When substance and function penetrate one another, there is no difference between demon and Buddha. All these mountains..."
There is a temple. Where is there that is not one's home?
[The Master] ascends the hall: "Last night I dreamed of Linji and Deshan; their blows fell like a shower of rain and their shouts roared like thunder.
When I opened my eyes, it was merely a storm of rain and thunder. Today, as I ascend the hall, I relate this to the assembly: the majesty of these two great elders..."
The spiritual aura and blazing flames are vividly present before our eyes. Have you all ever seen them in a dream?
If not, then on a day when thunder and rain crash together, one or two of you will suffer so deeply it penetrates the very marrow of your bones, and your skulls will be shattered by the roar.
Do not mistakenly blame me for being too harsh at Jiangshan.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "This mind is still not yet resolved; even a drop of water is difficult to digest. Now tell me, what is this mind?
He then struck the meditation seat once and said: "If you all were to resolve it right here, spending ten thousand taels of gold every day would not be considered excessive.
Why, then, did the Patriarch Baizhang say: 'As for those who spend ten thousand taels of gold every day, I..."?
"It does not abide here. Tell me, where does the crux lie? After a long silence, he said: "A vast marsh conceals the mountain; its principle can subdue the leopard.
He ascended the hall and said: "To affirm it is an error; to deny it is still deviant. One blow and the myriad heavy locks open; Old Lu [Huineng]..."
He turned the phrase around and said, "The bright mirror is not the stand.

He then ascended the hall and said: "There has never been a mind without an object, nor has there ever been an object without a mind. When the ancients gave such a report, people scratched their heads, not knowing where the itch lay.
Even if both mind and object were empty, there would still come a day when one must wear an iron collar and carry a saddle. Suddenly, he picked up his whisk.
The Master addressed the great assembly, saying: "This is the objective realm (*viṣaya*). What do you call the mind? After a long silence, he said:
"Since then, one does not return; yet when one returns, it is attained. Amidst the misty waves of the Five Lakes, who can vie for it?"
In the *Recorded Sayings* of Xuefeng Chongsheng Chan Temple, it says regarding the Main Gate:
"Only those who possess eyes that can discern with certainty from three thousand miles away may enter this gate.
If you have not yet reached such a state, then simply follow behind the new Elder’s heels."
In the Buddha Hall, he burns incense and says: "I and the Old Man Śākyamuni share an enmity that cannot be borne under the same sky.
Why, then, do I burn incense and prostrate today? It is not without reason that enemies meet."
The Abbot took his seat and said: "Under the gate of the Patriarchs, the path of men is cut off; its depth and peril exceed those of a ten-thousand-fathom pit.

To stretch out a hand here is but a waste of effort; let the green moss grow upon the hall as it will. Even so, the official way admits not even a needle, yet the private way allows for carriages and horses."
He ascends the seat. Having finished offering incense to pray for the Emperor, he next holds up the incense and says: "The seal of Mian was extremely tight, yet its fame spread ever further;
though the source of the Cao River had not been reached, its value increased tenfold. I burn this toward the furnace so that all who hear may be universally benefited."
[The Master] treated them all as adversaries. He then adjusted his robes and took his seat.
A monk asked, "Having traveled far from Zhongfu to arrive at Xuefeng, what is the Venerable One of Immovability? The Master said, "Forty days on the road.
The monk pressed further, "Truly excellent is the Venerable One of Immovability! The Master said, "Setting out early and arriving late for lodging. The monk pressed again.
"I know that the Master is accustomed to using this device. The Master said, "Why do you not understand it? He replied, "This is precisely where I, your student, find my strength.
The Master said, "You cannot deceive the eyes of the new Elder. He replied, "What was it like before the Master had seen Cao Yuan?
The Master said, "In Zhangzhou, Quanzhou, and Fujian, people have flat heads like fans. He replied, "How is it after having seen [the source]? The Master said, "Just as before."
"What? the Master said. "One may only hear his name; one must not see his face. The monk pressed on:
"Setting aside for a moment the question of seeing or not seeing, how would you speak the single phrase for the Emperor’s longevity upon opening the hall today? The Master said:
"When one person has cause for celebration, the myriad people depend upon it. The monk said: "If that is so, then I shall know gratitude and repay it," and he prostrated himself. The Master then—

It is said: "Master Zeng sat firmly atop Elephant Bone Peak, allowing not even a drop of water to pass through. Master Bao did not descend from the summit of Mount Zhongshan, yet came to claim its territory.

With staff, ruler, and compass always by his side, this world and all other realms were brought under his command. Having brought them under his command, he exercised freedom in both bestowing and taking away;
the Dharma followed the practice of the Dharma, and the banner of the Dharma was erected wherever he went. Thus it is said: 'To establish the Dharma...'"
"The banner stands firm; the fundamental principle is clearly the Buddha’s mandate from Caoxi.

When the ancients gave such a report, it was much like instructing people in a village of three households to follow the vermilion lines—who would not know how? Whether one knows or not, Biancai’s jade is flawless and the dragon pearl is free of blemish.
"The Dharma banner and the fundamental principle are the Buddha’s mandate from Caoxi. [He] strikes the meditation seat once and says: "All point toward this very place."
All at once, it is ground to powder. What a fine world of peace and tranquility! To go about in this very manner, the grace of the Emperor and the grace of the Buddha are both repaid at once.

The Way of the Sovereign and the Way of the Patriarchs proceed together without contradiction. Do not say there are few who understand in this world; that family naturally has those who appreciate it.
Again, he raised an example: One day the World-Honored One ascended the seat. Mañjuśrī struck the gavel and said: "Behold clearly."
The Dharma-method of the Dharma King is thus. When the World-Honored One descended from his seat, the Master said: "The World-Honored One abandoned himself to follow others;

Mañjuśrī followed the heterodox and pursued evil. At that time, had there been someone among the assembly of a million who had come forth, slapping their hands and laughing loudly, one could have guaranteed that Mañjuśrī would not even have been able to strike the gavel, nor would the World-Honored One have been able to descend from his seat. Furthermore—
The Way. Where does the confusion lie? Try to discern it! That evening, he gave a small *can*:
"A man of seventy years still grasps the handle of another's ladle. Having traversed three thousand li, how many mountains and rivers have been crossed?
This mountain monk stayed in Jinling for fourteen years; I have gathered some playthings. Several times..."
The waist-bag could not hold it all; several times he attempted to carry it in a basket, but it was difficult to fit.
He had no choice but to transport it by way of the sea route, intending to perform as the occasion required before the Great Peak (Dading Feng).

Little did he expect that a gust of karmic wind would blow him into the mountains of Xuefeng. Upon careful inspection, one finds that everything transported by sea has already been used up by others throughout the various quarters.

Section. One cannot avoid relying on an established precedent to respond to the present occasion. Before the sacred arrow has even been released, everyone within the nine-layered capital looks up in expectation;
while the three armies remain motionless, who does not travel together along that single path through the night?
When you all hear this, you will surely break into cold laughter. But what if, suddenly, the sacred arrow were snapped and twisted?
Turning the corner, he lets loose a single "tortoise-nose" from the South Mountain, swallowing up the entire universe and the great earth—sentient and insentient alike—in a single gulp.
If there were someone among the assembly who possessed a way to turn themselves around and find their own living path, only then would it be truly laughable.
Even so, Vipaśyin Buddha set his mind upon this long ago, yet until this very day, he has not attained its wondrous essence.
Again, Xuefeng addressed the assembly, saying: "I have already met you at Wushan Ridge;
I have already met you at Wangzhou Pavilion; I have already met you before the Sangha Hall. Baofu asked Ehu: "..."
"Let us set aside for now the matter before the Sangha Hall. At which place do you meet [us] at Wushan Ridge or Wangzhou Pavilion?
Guo-hu suddenly took a swift step back toward his quarters. Baofu entered the Sangha Hall. The Master said, "Xuefeng hangs the 'Poisonous Drum';
he only seeks someone capable of untying it. Guo-hu and Baofu join hands together; with a single casual strike, all who hear it shall perish. The assembly...
Is there anything living within it? Let me ask you: at which place do you meet at Wushili and Wangzhouting?
Everyone, please offer a turning word.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Thrown high, it does not reach the heavens; cast low, it does not touch the earth. There is no place to hide, north, south, east, or west.
It brings shame upon the old man Xuefeng, who called it the 'tortoise-nose of the South Mountain.'"
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the case of Attendant Shan. While at Dayu Zhi’s place, during a session of entering the room, Dayu kicked out a single sandal.
Attendant Shan withdrew and stood there. Dayu bent down to pick up the sandal; Attendant Shan gave it a kick and knocked it over.
Dayu then turned his back to the wall. [Master] Dianjin wrote three times on the wall; Attendant Shan stood staring behind him. Dayu—

He turned his body to take up his sandals and went straight to the Dharma Hall. A good attendant said, "To act for others in such a manner will surely blind the eyes of the people in this entire city.
The Master said, "Dagui issued an order that could not be disobeyed; I acted according to that order."
An excellent attendant may encounter a situation where something ought to be severed but is not; one must sever it in accordance with the occasion.
If one lets it pass, both are masters of the craft; if one scrutinizes it, both fall into a trap. Let those with the true eye discern this.
Ascending the hall: The Buddha is ten feet high; the Mara is ten feet high. The moon falls into the cold pond; clouds arise from the green cliffs.
Failing to recognize Maitreya Tathāgata, they call him the Bagua (Cloth Sack) Monk.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised an ancient case: A monk visited Xuefeng. Xuefeng asked, “Where have you come from?
The monk said, “From Zhejiang. Xuefeng asked, “By boat or by land? The monk said, “I have not traveled either way. Xuefeng said, “How did you get here? The monk said, “What obstacle could there be?
Xuefeng struck him and drove him out. Ten years later, the monk came again. Xuefeng asked, “Where have you come from? The monk...
The monk said, "I come from Hunan. Feng asked, "How far is it from Hunan to here? The monk said, "Not separated by anything.
Feng raised his whisk and asked, "Is it separated by this? The monk said, "If it were separated, how could I have reached here? Feng struck him and drove him out again.
The Master said, "With Hongya [the cliff] hundreds of feet high in front and white blades clashing behind, how can one enter?"
Having entered the gate of Xuefeng, this monk, after taking up residence there, would invariably curse Xuefeng whenever he saw anyone.
The Master said, "This monk knows only how to step forward, but does not realize there is a thorn beneath his feet. Later, a fellow practitioner who had heard of this went specifically to visit him.
The Master then asked, "For what reason did you revile Xuefeng? The monk then recounted the two previous incidents.
The Master said, "That monk has been dead for a long time; even if he could be brought back to life by your pointing it out, what use would that be?
Thereupon, the monk wept bitterly. Every midnight, he would burn incense and prostrate himself toward Xuefeng. The Master [observed this].
It is truly pitiable and painful! At that time, after being exposed by his companion, he should have immediately cursed Xuefeng and driven him out along with his companion;
only then would he not have disgraced Old Man Xuefeng. When I, this mountain monk, report it thus, what is my intention?
"If one lacks such an eye for selecting a Buddha, even a thousand years would be of no avail."
The Record of the Chan Monastery Tian Tong Jing De in Qing Yuan Prefecture.
On the third day of the tenth month in the third year of the Jia Xi era (1239), the year of Ji Hai, he entered the monastery.
Pointing to the triple-gate, he said: "Entering through this gate, there is nothing that is not as it is; exiting, every single person returns to the source. For what reason..."
"Ma! Not knowing where the path begins or ends—having no place to land—one goes when one wishes to go and stays when one wishes to stay.
[At the Buddha Hall, while burning incense: "The patch-robed monks do not seek the Buddha, nor do they seek the Dharma. And yet, even though this is so..."
Amidst the smoke and flames of others, how would one dare not bow the head?

Sitting upon the square measure (the abbot’s seat), he said: "Before this mountain monk has even left Fucheng, I have already put on my straw sandals and traveled hundreds and thousands of turns within the bellies of all of you.
What more is there to seek here for a bowl? Nevertheless, though it is so, [I am] ten parts complete."
This accords with human sentiment. Yet, for a mountain monk on the Way, there is no expedient means.
He takes up the imperial decree and shows it to the assembly, saying:

"If we discuss this matter, it is like the Sage Emperor who issues a single proclamation or a single edict; throughout the four quarters and the eight reaches, there is none that does not submit in obedience. Furthermore, he requests the Rector...
He revealed it directly before him.
Pointing to the Dharma seat, he said: "Wherever the tips of one's toes reach, the four quarters and eight directions are entirely free of obstruction;

as soon as the living path is opened, the myriad distinctions and thousandfold differences are all cut off. Who can perceive this with the eye that strikes before the pivot? He then ascended the seat and, holding up incense, offered a prayer.

The Master concluded the formal session. Next, he held up the incense and said: "Before the Peak of Kāśyapa and within the waves of the Cao Source, I take it up with my hand; there is neither right nor wrong.
I burn it in the incense burner, desiring only that you all have a sudden flash of realization. (Question and answer not recorded). The Master then said:

"The Way is fundamentally a single thread, yet its application encompasses the myriad differences. Yesterday in Southern Min, I was called the Elder of Xuefeng; today having come to Eastern Zhejiang, I am thus..."
As the master of Tiantong, though we come and go across a distance of three thousand li, whether here or there, there is not even a hair’s breadth of separation between us.
When the ladle is set down, the fifteen hundred virtuous teachers have no place to put their bodies;
when the sack is opened, the thousand-billion-fold transformation-body Maitreya manifests the responsive mechanism to meet sentient beings. Thus it is.

If you proceed in this manner, the school of Bodhidharma will be wiped out like dust. Before you stands an assembly that is entirely composed of highly realized masters of profound training—monks who roam freely throughout the world.

If you can fix a single living eye here, you may assist in the sage-like transformation of the era of Tang and Yu and transmit the wondrous mind of the Buddhas and Patriarchs; thus, the monastic communities will see their value increase tenfold. Why is this so?
The roots are firmly established beneath the lair of the fish-dragons; the atmosphere is lofty at the rim of the sun and moon wheels. Again, he raised the case:
When Baoshou opened the hall for his first sermon, Sansheng pushed forward a monk. Baoshou struck him immediately.
Sansheng said, "If you act as a teacher in this manner, you will not only blind this monk's eyes, but you will blind the eyes of the entire city of Zhenzhou. Baoshou then cast down his staff.
He returned to the abbot’s quarters. The Master said, “Baoshou held the scales in his hand and exercised the sovereign’s power of life and death.
Had it not been for the Three Sages’ profound discernment of the subtle nuances, how could the merit of his great achievements have been seen?
Yet he was exposed by this monk. Tell me, where exactly did this monk catch him out? After a long silence, he said, “This melody should belong only to the heavens; no one on earth can sing it.”
How many times has one heard this in the interim?

That evening, he gave a small discourse (xiaocan): "In years past, I went there in person; carrying my staff, I counted tens of thousands of pine trees. Today I return once more; in the snap of a finger, forty years have passed.
Although the times have shifted and affairs have changed, alas, the environment and my spirit remain in harmonious fusion. By the side of the pond...
The gulls and egrets still recognize their old master; the mountains and rivers outside the gate still present their former faces.
Unable to avoid entering the Treasury of Radiance and sitting upon the Peak of Mount Sumeru, he unleashes the Great Icchantika and employs the Seal of the Demon King.

He takes all Buddhas and Patriarchs of the past, the entire world of heaven and earth, and all things sentient and insentient, and seals them all with a single seal, such that there is not a single hair’s breadth of difference. Not one...
Not even a hair’s breadth of shared characteristics—just go like this. In years past, you went, yet you never truly arrived; today you come again, yet fundamentally you do not come.
Whether arriving or not arriving, whether coming or not coming—at every place is Maitreya; where there is no gate, there is no Sudhana.
Again, Master Qishi of Mount Dang was asked by a monk: "A student has come here with a direct purpose; I ask the Master for a direct response.
Master Qishi said, "Right here, one simply defecates and finishes. What need is there to speak of 'direct' or 'purposeful'?

The Master [Zhaozhou] said, "Seize the thief’s spear to kill the thief; ride the thief’s horse to pursue the thief. The monk said, "If you, Master, answer questions in this way, you will have to buy more straw sandals."
"Only through traveling on foot can one attain it. The Master said: "If you are not one who plays in the tide, do not enter the surging waves.
He called to a monk, "Come forward! When the monk drew near, the Master struck him. The Master said: "A good blow!
It must be until all the people of the great earth have eaten this staff that Tiantong may finally be established. Let those with eyes discern this!
Ascending the hall: Six windows and closed doors still leave behind traces of absolute illumination; four crossroads with no people yet linger the marks of sunken emptiness.
Illumination leaves no trace, emptiness leaves no mark—thus did Bodhidharma face the wall, and Yunmen spoke of "the seventh."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: Linji asked a newly arrived monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Luancheng. Linji said, "May I ask you something?
The monk said, "I am a novice and do not understand. Linji said, "In the entire land of the Great Tang, could one find anyone who does not understand?
Go to the meditation hall! The Master said: "There is a dose of cummin seed in the rice. At that time, Xinghua was...
The attendant asked Daowei, "Regarding that newcomer just now, did you strip him of his status or not? Daowei said, "Who am I to concern myself with whether he is stripped or not?
Xinghua said, "The Master only knows how to pick up a dead sparrow and flick it on the ground;
he does not know how to use a turning phrase to cover it over. The Master said, "The father stole the sheep, and the son testified to it."
Ji said, "How about you? Huazhou replied, "I request the Master to act as the newly arrived guest. Ji said, "A new precept-holder does not understand.
Huazhou said, "Rather, this is my own fault, Old Monk. Ji said, "Your words conceal the point. As Huazhou hesitated, Ji struck him.
Ji then struck him. The Master said, "Xinghua intended to share the spoils with the 'white-handed thief,' yet he could not escape from Linji's hand.

That evening, Linji said to Xinghua, "Today when I questioned the newcomer, it was like 'poking a dying sparrow on the ground' or 'beating it right in its nest. But as soon as you produced a word, I shouted and drove him away. Regarding this:
[The Master] struck him amidst the blue clouds. The Master said, "Out of pity for one's son, one does not notice their ugliness. Xinghua said, "The grass-thief has been utterly defeated.
The Master said, "When the family is prosperous, filial sons are born. Jie then struck him. The Master said, "That was not yet the fodder of the fundamental division.
Where has that staff gone—the one which, when you were with Huangbo, was like a whisk made of thistle branches? He then called to the assembly.
It is said: "The son’s stratagem of delusion seizes the father’s opportunity. These two great elders compared their skills, yet they could not avoid letting this monk slip away.
Let those with the eye of discernment distinguish it.

Ascending the hall, he said: "There is one person who, in a single thought-moment, attains sudden realization and falls among the ranks of the Buddhas. There is another person who, for kalpas on end, remains an icchantika, having no wish to become a Buddha.
Now tell me, which of these two deserves the offerings of devas and humans? After a long silence, he said: "A butterfly pierces the fragrant path, its two brows damp;
a bee plunders the withered flower, its two thighs stout."
Ascending the hall, he took up his staff and addressed the assembly, saying: "Deshan’s staff was like falling raindrops; every blow pierced to the very marrow of the bones.
Linji’s shout was like a rolling thunderclap; every roar shattered the skull. There are a certain kind of people who, upon hearing such accounts, are like the wind passing through trees.
Yet, the gate of a skilled physician is where the most patients gather. Today, Tiantong shall further provide a funeral service for them."
The Horse Doctor. [Zhaozhou] struck his staff once, gave a shout, and descended from the seat.
When Master Quan addressed the assembly at Yuyang, he said: "What Tian Tong used is not applicable here at Yuyang; what I use here at Yuyang is not applicable back at Tian Tong.
Nevertheless, where it is not applicable, its utility is more than sufficient—like an arrow that brings down two eagles."
It fell from his hand as he spoke.
He ascended the hall and said: "Makhadeva shut away his room; Vimalakīrti sealed his mouth. The heavenly net is vast and wide—loose, yet nothing slips through.
You people here, how will you penetrate it?"
Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "The functioning of the Buddhas and Patriarchs of the past is like the violent wind and sudden rain, the swift thunder and flashing lightning of the other day.
Its majestic spirit and blazing intensity—no one knows from whence it comes; those who see it cannot help but be struck with awe.

Yet when, after a short while, the wind ceases and the rain clears, the blue sky and bright sun reveal their clarity to all. No one realizes that within this very clarity lies such immense majesty and spiritual power."
"Flame! Furthermore, where does it go? In such an application, this mountain monk has a little bit [of understanding] as well.
I do not wish to recklessly communicate the message; wait until the time of the next sudden gale and torrential rain, and you all must quickly open your eyes."
Ascending the hall, he raised the following case: A monk visited Master Pingtian. Pingtian struck him once with his staff.
The monk stepped forward and seized the staff. Pingtian said, "I was too hasty just now. The monk then struck Pingtian once with the staff.
Pingtian said, "An adept! An adept! The monk bowed. Pingtian seized the monk and said, "It was you, Dharma brother, who were hasty."
The monk laughed heartily. Pītān said, "This monk has met with defeat today.
The Master said, "When the host shows the intention of having a good guest, even in seizing and taking away, one does not lose what is appropriate.

When the guest maintains the mind of honoring the host, every advance and retreat must follow the rules of propriety. As for Pītān saying, 'This monk has met with defeat today,' what was his intention?"
If the price is not paid, one must dispute over what is true and what is false.
Entering the hall, he raised the case of Master Xiangyan, who addressed the assembly, saying:

"It is like a person on a thousand-foot precipice, with a tree branch in his mouth, having nothing for his hands to grasp and nothing for his feet to tread upon. Suddenly someone asks about the meaning of the Westward Journey; if he does not answer, he violates [the truth];"
When asked by another, if one were to answer, one would lose both body and life. At such a time, what should be done?
At that moment, the Venerable Tuhou said, "I do not ask about having climbed the tree; please, Master, speak before climbing it. Xiangyan laughed heartily. Xuedou commented:
"The Dharma emerges and craftiness arises; the command is issued and deception springs up. Xuedou also said: "Speak from atop the tree."
"The easy path is beneath the tree; the difficult path is upon it. An old monk is climbing the tree. He then posed a question:
"To manipulate words and play with the Dharma is not the mark of a true adept. As for Xiangyan’s great laughter—what was his intention?
I ask you all now to offer a turning word."
Ascending the hall, he said: "One who sits and cuts off the lands of the ten directions, the one who is uniquely honored above heaven and below heaven—such a person cannot take even a single step.
One who swallows the Buddhas of the three periods of time, penetrating both the mundane and the supramundane—such a person cannot utter even a single word."
Nevertheless, even so, it is fit to serve as a model for monks. What is Puhua like? He is just a donkey.
Linji was not yet a "white-handed thief.
[He] ascended the hall and said: "All the Buddhas and Patriarchs of the past, and all the venerable elders throughout the world who have appeared in this world, have all upheld this very matter."
"Using a female messenger to seek a dove; baiting a hook to catch fish. Here in this mountain monk’s place, there is no such leisurely business.
Do any of you here have that which is self-awakened without a teacher?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "There is a thing that cannot be named, cannot be described, cannot be grasped, and cannot be relinquished.

Changning Zhijun Wenzhong’s *Exhortation to Preach Universally* (the name Fu-zhi, style name Ting-rui):

There are no two paths in the world, and no two minds in the Sage. Since there are no two paths and no two minds, there is not a single dharma that is not the True Vehicle, and not a single matter that does not constitute a wondrous function. This is why Gautama cultivated himself by means of this.
The mind. Lao Dan cultivated his nature by means of this; Niqiu governed his person by means of this.

There is not one who does not proceed from this path of non-duality and this mind of non-duality. To speak according to reality: for one who cultivates the mind, when they reach the point where there is nothing further to cultivate, they are no longer obstructed by the mind.
For one who nourishes their nature, when they reach the point where there is nothing further to nourish, they are no longer [obstructed] by nature.
Those who cultivate the body reach the state where there is nothing further to be cultivated; thus they are no longer burdened by the body.
Being unburdened by the body, they are not constrained by nature, nor obstructed by the mind. Their entire being is the non-dual Way and the non-dual mind.
Within this, the twenty-five realms of existence throughout the three worlds are, in that very moment, leveled and submerged.

The eighty-four thousand afflictions are liberated according to their respective locations. Thus, regarding this path of non-duality and the mind of non-duality, before one has attained thorough clarity, there has never been a lack of even a single hair’s breadth;
once thorough clarity has been attained, there has likewise never been an increase of even a single hair’s breadth.
Know that this matter is inherently possessed by every person and is perfectly accomplished in each and every one; it is simply a matter of being able to...
When mindfulness suddenly transcends, the fruition of realization is naturally attained.

If you have not yet attained this fruition of realization, you must, throughout the twelve periods of the day—whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down—attend closely with your eyes wherever you encounter conditions in daily life, amidst the entanglement of right and wrong, and in all states of adversity and favor, whether horizontal or vertical.
This is because you have not yet clarified the Way of non-duality; from what source does that single thought-moment at the bottom of the non-dual mind arise?
Come! Suddenly, you will clearly perceive this single thought, like encountering an old friend in a bustling marketplace;
his former bearing appears vividly before you, without needing to ask anyone, as your own mind is perfectly clear. Thereafter, you will respond to conditions throughout your daily life.
Right and wrong, opposition and compliance—all these are one’s own home. The samādhi of self-enjoyment, the Way of non-duality, and the mind of non-duality are entirely contained herein.

The mind of birth and death is shattered; once the life-root is severed and all technicalities forgotten, one proceeds directly upward toward the crown of the Buddhas and Patriarchs.
There, one sees Śākyamuni holding up the flower and Kāśyapa smiling—what a matter of great leisure!
Only then will you know that Dizang and Fayan remain sitting in the grass until this day, unable to raise their heads. If you can examine this and bring it forth, [you shall truly understand].
I, this mountain monk, have never uttered so much as a single word or character. If this is not yet the case, you must strictly avoid falling into the trap of verbal patterns.

What is the ultimate point? At such a time, let alone this mountain monk and you venerable seniors failing to find our heads and noses, even if a thousand sages and ten thousand saints were to appear with three heads and six arms, they would still have no way to enter.

He walked away with his arms swinging. Then, striking the left side of the rope bed with his whisk, he said:
"If you see through here thoroughly, you are the Host from beginning to end. Striking the right side of the rope bed with the whisk, he said:
"If you see through here thoroughly, you are the Guest from beginning to end. Tapping once in the middle with the whisk, he said: "If you see through here thoroughly—"
Go! The guest is the host; the host is the guest. Guest and host interpenetrate; their application is unimpeded—truly, their application is unimpeded.
Piṇḍola daily accepts offerings from the four continents, yet he never leaves his own place and remains eternally serene.
When the Treasure Lord of the Liang dynasty manifested as the Twelve-Faced Avalokiteśvara, you knew well enough that he was no ordinary monk. Do you all, however, know?
As for the final resting places of Jiangshan and Huqiu—both of these elders were merely "barbarian kings. Who in the world understands how to appreciate their true sound?
I, the Mountain Man, have sat upon Mount Zhong for nine years; as drought and flooding followed one another, the assembly suffered from a lack of food.

Consequently, I descended the mountain to carry the alms bowl, seeking a means to provide for our sustenance. I am deeply indebted to my elder brother at Huqiu, who commanded me to act on behalf of the community.
Speaking of the East while talking of the West—though my understanding of the Way is shallow, I dare not stubbornly decline the honor of this solemn command.
I can do no more than borrow my elder brother’s nostrils to breathe, responding to the needs of the moment. As my elder brother said to the assembly:
"Tiger Hill has nothing worth taking; it possesses only three turning words that test all people under heaven, neither of this age nor of antiquity. May I ask, Great...?
Assembly, what are the Three Turnings of the Word at Tiger Hill? Those of long-standing training among the former worthies would know them upon a single mention;

but for those of later learning and beginners, how can they penetrate and clearly understand them? You must know that these three turnings of the word have been used by all Buddhas and Patriarchs of the past, as well as by the old monks throughout the land, to respond to the world.
The heavens and earth, the great realm, the sun, moon, and stars, and the myriad phenomena...

The myriad phenomena—form and emptiness, light and darkness—are established by this. The four types of noble beings and the six classes of ordinary beings, both sentient and insentient, emerge and submerge by this.
Brothers, as long as you have not yet penetrated the three turning phrases, you will be deceived by all the Buddhas and Patriarchs of the past, as well as the old monks throughout the world;
even the heavens and earth, the sun, moon, and stars, and the dense array of the myriad phenomena, form and emptiness... [are all so deceived].
Brightness and darkness are deceived. The four noble ones and the six classes of ordinary beings, sentient and insentient alike, are all deceived.

Since each and every one is deceived, how can these three turning words be made manifest? It can only be so if, during the twelve periods of the day, within the four modes of deportment, at all times and in all places—whether in motion or stillness, in speech or silence—one’s own three hundred and sixty bones [are awakened].
The Juncture. From the eighty-four thousand pores of the skin, extending throughout the entirety of heaven and earth, at this very moment all are clearly manifesting these three turning words.
Thus, one attains a state where mind follows mind without interval and never forgets them; as days pass and years deepen...
Meeting circumstances and encountering conditions, one strikes and bumps against them; it is like a collapsing cliff or a falling rock, resembling the crumbling of heaven and the cracking of earth.
In a single moment, one sees that all the Buddhas and Patriarchs of antiquity and the elder monks of the world seek their lives within one’s hands.

Throughout the great earth of heaven and earth, the sun, moon, and stars, the myriad phenomena of the forested and the vast, form and emptiness, light and darkness—nowhere can they take root. The four sages...

The six classes of ordinary beings, the sentient and the insentient—all perish at once. Only then do you believe that the Buddhas and Patriarchs of the past and the old monks of the world cannot deceive you;
that heaven and earth, the great land, the sun, moon, and stars, the myriad phenomena of the forest and the mountains, form and emptiness, light and darkness, cannot deceive you;
and that the four types of sages and the six classes of ordinary beings, the sentient and the insentient, cannot deceive you. Why is this? It is because...

From the Buddhas and Patriarchs above, down to the old monks of the world, and including the four sages and six classes of beings—sentient and insentient alike—all flow forth from these three turning words. Thus it is said: "The Buddhas and all sentient beings all receive this power of grace;
once this power of grace is recognized, sentient beings are cut off from all news. Nevertheless, tell me: what of these three?
A turning word: from what source does it flow forth? You must know that our elder brother, Master Xueqiu, has transmitted this since the time of the Bequeathal at Vulture Peak;
thus, it flows from his own breast, encompassing heaven and earth. Yet, alas, the land is vast and people are few; those who encounter it are rare.
Have you not seen how, in the past, when Xuefeng was dwelling in a hermitage, a monk came to visit him, and Xuefeng simply pressed the monk with his hand against the hut?
The Gatekeeper asked, "What is it? The monk also said, "What is it? Xuefeng lowered his head and returned to his hut.
Xuefeng had casually revealed a mere glimpse of what is before one's eyes—like an inch of iron held in hand, yet everywhere are swords and spears.
It was simply that this monk could not grasp the handle. Had he grasped the handle, where would there be a Xuefeng? The monk then took his leave of Xuefeng, who asked him: [The text ends here.]
Xuefeng asked, "Where are you going? The monk said, "I am going to Hunan. Xuefeng said, "I have a fellow practitioner who lives at Yantou;
send him this message. The monk said, "Please give me Xuefeng’s message. Xuefeng said, "Ever since attaining the Way at Aoshan, until now, he has been full and never hungry.
"Brothers," [the Master continued,] "this is how Yantou and Xuefeng took their leave of Deshan. When they arrived at...
At the Aoshan Inn, there was an occasion for being detained by the snow.
Observe how those ancients were so earnest in their pursuit of the Way that even in a solitary village or a humble inn, they kept this Way in mind. Yantou stretched out his two legs and slept;
tell me, where does his intention lie? Xuefeng sat in meditation in a heap of snow; where did he direct his attention? Yantou said: "Eating and sleeping."

"Go! He is just like the local deity of the seven villages; at some other time or occasion, he will go about bewitching the men and women of people's homes. Thus one knows that through constant polishing and refining, and by means of deep prodding and piercing pain, unless one possesses great eyes and is a fellow traveler on the Way, how could one admonish and warn so urgently?

Since Xuefeng had been struck by Yantou at his most painful point— [The text continues with the narrative of Xuefeng’s realization. ...Xuefeng attained great enlightenment. He then went to see Dongshan, who asked him, "Where have you come from? Xuefeng replied, "I have just left Yantou. Dongshan said, "What did he say to you? This is why it is said: "To know the place where the axe-head meets the handle, one must first pass through the gate of the Great Death. This is what is meant by "the great matter of life and death. It is not something to be sought through intellectual understanding or verbal expression; it is a matter of direct realization. If one does not possess the eye of a true patriarch, how can one ever grasp this? It is for this reason that the ancient masters used such fierce methods to cut through delusion and reveal the fundamental source. One must personally experience this for oneself; it cannot be transmitted through words. This is the ultimate teaching of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. How could it be otherwise? It is a matter of life and death, the very marrow of one's bones. If one does not encounter a true teacher and undergo such a transformation, one will remain lost in the cycle of birth and death. Therefore, do not take these words lightly. They are the vital instructions for those who wish to enter the Way. One must practice them with all one's heart and soul. This is the essential meaning of the ancestral teachings. Do not let it be lost. "Second: Throughout the twelve periods of the day, can you still maintain this state or not? Yantou said, "If it is like that, you have not even mastered saving yourself.

The Assembly: Ever since Xuefeng heard the meaning of "form is emptiness," witnessed Dongshan’s verse on crossing the water, and experienced his awakening beneath Deshan’s staff, he had attained points of realization.
Yet, alas, a single film remained in his eye, causing empty flowers to fall in confusion.

At that time, had it not been for Yantou—who possessed the needle for the vital organs and the means to revive those facing certain death—how could there have been that extraordinary episode at the Aoshan Inn?
Therefore, Xinxin says: "From the time he attained the Way at Mount Ao until the present day, he has been full and never hungry.
This too is like a poor child yearning for old debts. Yantou then asked the monk, "What further words or phrases did Xuefeng have?"
The monk recounted the previous conversation. Yantou asked, "What did Xuefeng say? The monk replied, "He was speechless and bowed his head before returning to his hut.

"Return to the hermitage and understand it there. Since this monk could not realize it, at the end of summer he requested further instruction from Yantou.
